STRUCT-01.title: Smurfing ring feeding a consultant's account
STRUCT-01.description: Five young customers deposit $9.0k-$9.9k cash at different branches and forward it the same day to Victor Hale, who also deposits just under $10k himself; proceeds are wired to a recently formed Varnholm trading company.

MULE-01.title: Student mule ring cashing out scam victims via crypto
MULE-01.description: Seven newly onboarded students share two phones, one IP and a flat; elderly customers send them 'investment' payments that are forwarded within hours to Ronan Pike, who wires the pool to a crypto exchange. The recruiter's phone and Pike's number were reported by Beta Credit Union.

CAROUSEL-01.title: Four same-director shells cycling funds
CAROUSEL-01.description: Four LLCs formed within a month share a Varnholm registered address and a single director; they pass roughly $50k around a closed loop four times, generating fake turnover.

SANCT-01.title: Supplier blocked under the 50% rule via layered ownership
SANCT-01.description: Bluefin pays Aurora Maritime, which is not listed itself but is 30% owned by designated Grigor Malenko and 25% by Northstar Holdings, wholly owned by designated Selene Group: 55% aggregate blocked ownership. Coral Freight (40%) is below the threshold but warrants enhanced due diligence.

LAYER-01.title: Seed 'investment' split across new accounts and parked offshore
LAYER-01.description: A six-week-old consultancy receives two ~$185k wires from a Qastria fund, splits each across three newly opened individual accounts within hours, and they forward ~96% to two Varnholm trust companies the next day.

MULE-B-EARLY.title: Earlier wave of the same mule crew (already exited)
MULE-B-EARLY.description: Closed in September; included so cross-bank links have a source.
